page.name: Fintech & payments
page.metaDescription: One-time codes, transaction alerts and payment reminders over the messaging accounts you already own, with routing and pacing on SMS and receipts normalized wherever the provider reports them.
page.lede: In payments the message is often the product: a code that has to land before the session expires, an alert that proves a transaction happened, a reminder that keeps a subscription alive. Connect your own accounts, and the send path stops being the part you have to watch.

sections.h: The messages you cannot afford to lose
bullets: One-time passwords and step-up verification codes
p: These messages have hard deadlines. A code that arrives late is a failed login; a reminder that arrives twice looks like fraud. The platform therefore exposes pacing and per-number rate limits explicitly rather than hiding them behind a single auto-scaling counter.

sections.h: Throughput follows your numbers, not a hidden quota
p: Provider limits apply per sender number and per account, and a single application quota hides the constraint that actually blocks you. The console shows the limit that applies to each connected number, and pacing is applied at that granularity — so adding a second number genuinely doubles throughput instead of splitting the same allowance.

Regulatory obligations in financial services — record retention, disclosure wording, sector-specific rules — belong to you and to the provider carrying the traffic; they follow the duty, and the duty sits with you. On the SMS channel the platform’s part is the send path: routing, pacing, and a log that records what went out and what happened to it.

faq.q: Can a duplicate code be prevented?
faq.a: Not by the platform. There is no idempotency key on the send API, so a retried request sends a second message. Duplicate prevention belongs in the caller — the guide on idempotency explains why and what to do instead.

faq.q: Are codes delivered on the fastest channel?
faq.a: You choose the channel by which provider account you send through. The platform does not silently switch channel for you; on SMS it can switch between your connected provider accounts when one stops accepting traffic.

faq.q: Does the platform store the content of the messages we send?
faq.a: No. The message log retains metadata only — time, destination, provider, sender identity, status and error code. Message bodies are not persisted, so content does not accumulate in a log you would later have to govern.
